reasoning_traces.think:
The core primitive is the additive summation of player-level missed tackles (primitive 1), which forms a linear projection of individual defensive failures onto team performance. This operator is structurally dual to offensive success metrics like yards after contact, creating a closed system of run-defense duality. The ranking (primitive 2) introduces discrete topology, turning continuous sum data into ordinal signals that are robust to scale changes but brittle at rank crossings. The worst-three cluster (primitive 3) isolates extreme cases where defensive systems have collapsed, serving as early warning indicators for coaching interventions. The broken tackle gap (primitive 4) highlights a critical information asymmetry: while defenders know their own misses, the public only observes half the story. This veto condition ensures that models do not overfit to incomplete data, maintaining anti-collinearity with offensive metrics. Historically, this approach traces back to early NFL efficiency studies in the 1980s, evolving through Sabermetrics in baseball and now applied to football's complex state spaces.
